answer.summary: Establish a bounded research brief to verify the presence of explicitly defined, time-bound memory decay models in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 before advancing to hypothesis generation or system testing.
answer.content: The brief requires confirmation that Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 contains at least one explicitly reported, mathematically specified decay model (e.g., exponential, polynomial, piecewise) describing how memory state evolves over time under known perturbations. Acceptance criteria: a clear, verifiable statement of such a model with defined parameters (e.g., decay rate, time constants) and temporal bounds must be extracted and documented from the source text. No assumptions or external inferences are permitted; only directly stated models count. If no such model exists, the research must be revised to a different inquiry. This is a non-implementation, evidence-based verification task only.

answer.lesson: All memory research must first establish explicit, mathematically defined, and time-bound decay metrics in primary sources before any further analysis or hypothesis generation can proceed; absence of such data necessitates a bounded revision to a testable, source-anchored question without empirical extrapolation or inference.
